rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Series** resistors share one current and add: R_s = R₁ + R₂ + ⋯ — larger than the largest. **Parallel** resistors share one voltage and add reciprocals: 1/R_p = Σ1/Rᵢ — smaller than the smallest. NEB 2021's trio (2, 3, 6 Ω across 12 V) collapses to 1 Ω drawing 12 A, verified branch by branch (6 + 4 + 2 A) — 4m. NEB 2024's pair (6 Ω, 3 Ω across 12 V) draws 2 A and 4 A with 6 A total (3m).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - R_s = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ - 1/R_p = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ - Two parallel: R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) - Wheatstone balance: P/Q = R/S

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Series: same current, shared voltage. Parallel: same voltage, shared current.**  ·  **Parallel resistance is smaller than the smallest branch** — more paths, easier flow.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: House wiring is parallel: every appliance gets the full mains voltage and works independently.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Two Ways to Wire Anything Every network, however tangled, reduces to series and parallel blocks. Series adds resistances; parallel adds conductances — and NEB 2021 and 2024 both tested the parallel rule with numericals.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2021, 2024) ### 2.1 Series Resistors end-to-end carry the **same current**; voltages add: $$R_s = R_1 + R_2 + R_3 + \cdots$$ — larger than the largest; used to divide voltage or limit current.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 99:** the rules operate on R = ρl/A values. - **To Topic 102:** a potential divider is a series pair tapping voltage. - **To capacitors (Topic 95):** the combination rules are exactly swapped.
